It was a cold night. A human scout ran through the plains, searching for interesting things. Grasses. Trees. Wind ripples the air - a storm had come through recently. No stars speckle the sky, no moons - only a faint outline of the other side of the inverted planet. The palace of the gods was a distant memory, high above the little people. He could hear booms from what sounded like shelling resonate through the planet, but nothing around him on the garden planet betrayed its nature. Nothing: that was what this planet simply was. No natural development, a stage for the gods to look down upon the little people and smile, nothing more than a target for the gods' rifles. What once was the zipping of sniper bullets and detonating of drones in the aerial sands now fell to dead silence in the night without stars, a night devoid of the comforting danger of the old Earth, here it was too perfect. Few if any predators, just plants as far as one could lay eyes upon. No wars, no strife, no conflict of any kind to motivate them to do better. If this was a book, it would be a Stephanie Meyer novel. Their story on this planet was one of fluff and filler - they had no place here on this perfect world. A gilded cage, a stage for the gods - one wonders if the militant anti-theists had it right all along. No bears, no wolves, no natural forces. Everything was plastic, everything had the consumerist stink of the ruined world they had fled from. Everything and nothing was real here. He came to a rock outcropping, and he ascended as he did every day, to gaze out upon the glades and fields, to try to catch a glimpse of Earth as he knew it as a child. None. Plastic and steel. Gods making a godless world. Something had changed, something was not right. A line in the distance, wrapping around the planet like the equator.
